title.narrative: Technical Cooperation and Capacity Building Facility (TECCBUF)

description.narrative: The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the effective implementation of EU's development cooperation within the Pacific ACP region in line with the Pacific Leaders' vision for inclusive development to achieve a region of peace, harmony, security and economic prosperity. TECCBUF also has a window for the funding of the EU-PIFS non-state actor programme, worth 2M EUR.

description.narrative: Enhanced policy dialogue and coordination between Pacific ACP States, the OCTs, CROP agencies, the DMRO, the EU and other development partners.
Annual number of oversight missions/ activities conducted which contributed to the implementation of the PRIP and TECCBUF programme.

comment.narrative: I annually
56 annually

Oversight activities have included the participation withinRegional SC meetings x1 annually TECCBUF PSC meetings x1 annuallyRIP and IntraACP funded Project Steering Committee meetings x5 annually not including quarterly technicalcoordination meetings and oversight meetings and missions undertaken virtually and in person. Inperson missions were not taken by TECCBUF during the July 2018 to December 2021 period due to limited number of staff as a result of recruitment challenges and staff turnover initially then COVID travel restrictions later. Ongoing RAO Helpdesk functions also significantly impacted staff availability for oversight missions.This indicator is recommended to include virtual missions i.e. virtual meetings with stakeholders in relation to implementation of EU programmes.

description.narrative: Improved capacities of Regional organizations and other relevant stakeholders at regional and national level in the Pacific region to implement EU programmes in light of joint commitments made under the SDGs and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.
Number of events/actions, including capacity building, supported in relation to SDGs and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change, CROP, and PRIP implementation support annually.

comment.narrative: 2 annually
5 annually

There was no dedicated SDG training supported during the 2018 to December 2021 period however support to areas of SDGs 5 10 13 14 and 17 includedPACP participation in international fora on climate change in line with Pacific advocacy on the Paris Agreement on Climate Change in line with SDG 13 and actions to combat climate change. This included providing partial support to Pacific delegation attendance at COP 26.Supporting USP Tuvalu Kiribati Nauru Fiji and Vanuatu attendance from their respective Ministries of Fisheries and Infrastructure to IMO meetings in London. This is towards SDG 14 for sustainably used oceans and marine resources.Supporting NSA capacity building and participation at national regional and international events. This is towards SDG 10 for reduced inequalities within and between countries and SDG 17 which strengthens partnerships and the means of implementation.Support toward Gender related activities under the NSA capacity building and participation. This is towards SDG 5 for gender equality and empowering women and girls.Capacity Building was provided to the NAOs in the form of ICT equipment to 15 countries. FIJI NAO were trained by TECCBUF Advisor and were the first NAO to receive their equipment in December 2021. This equipment allows additional avenues for better engagement during online meetings of NAOs and PACP leaders reduces the carbon footprint of participants in line with SDG 13 and actions to combat climate change. The equipment also supports SDG 17 which strengthens partnerships and the means of implementation.The 3 CROP support proposals which were approved for progress prior to 2021 also support SDG 17. During 2021 work on the Pillar Assessment proposal ceased after advice from the EUD. The Regional Tender Portal project implementation is currently in progress and the SPC driven Data Hub project anticipates early 2022 contract is signing.Going forward and retrospectively all trainings workshops and events planned are to be tracked for links to specific SDGs and action on the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. Feedback will be solicited from all supported participants for a full picture of the results in the 2022 Annual Report.

description.narrative: RAO better coordinates and steers the design and implementation of RIP and IntraACP funded actions in the Pacific region, and provides more effective oversight, monitoring and reporting.
Percentage of beneficiaries indicating that programming, implementation, ME oversight assistance and advice and procedural support that it facilitated EU programmes implementation.

comment.narrative: Cumulative

No formal feedback mechanisms were in place to capture specific feedback from beneficiaries however there are adhoc email and verbal feedback from participants expressing their gratitude to PIFS for the opportunity to engage in those dialogue spaces. Feedback via emails publications and posts on the social media and websites of beneficiaries and recipients will be collated for the the final report.A questionnaire was issued in previous phase of the programme and the data remained useful for TECCBUF. No survey or equivalent was circulated or poll taken during the July 2018 to December 2021 period however the following observations amongst others indicate the high level of involvement of ORAO and its Helpdesk towards successful EU programmes implementationConsultation negotiation and contractual aspects including amendments to AgreementsAssistance given to Stakeholder Agencies for the preparation finalization of 10 ADs and 9 Financing Agreements.Facilitation and support towards nomination of Implementing Agencies Delegation Agreements preparations and finalizations. % of ADs being drafted in consultation with relevant stakeholders including CSOs, and womens organizations during the consultations

comment.narrative: Although the logframes say the target is to be achieved by first quarter 2018 the Delegation Authority was not signed until 23072018.

100 of the 10 ADs which fed into the FAs were developed with wide consultation with relevant stakeholders including CSOs and womens organizations from their formulation. The ADs both at FA and Contract level were drafted with wide consultation between 2018 and 2021. In accordance with the agreed PRIP Implementation framework different Working Groups were formed following an open invitation to the relevant stakeholders in the region. The final members of the working Groups formed werePriority area 1 PRISE Technical Working Group TWG composed of PIFS EUD ADB SPTO USP SPC PIPSO UNCTAD MSG OCO and representative of 3 PACP countries PNG Tonga and Solomon Islands. This is coChaired by PIFS and SPC.Priority area 2PacWaste Partnership Programme TWG includes SPREP USP SPC EUD and other relevant technical stakeholders. This was Chaired by SPREP.PEUMP TWG includes SPC FFA USP LMMA IUCN EUD and others. This was Chaired by SPC.Priority Area 3PPEVAW Programme TWG includes UN Women SPC USP CSOs FEMM Link PIANGO EUD and others. Chaired by UN Women.PFM Programme TWG includes USP SPC PIFS UNDP IFM PASAI EUD and others. Chaired by PIFS.Health Support Programme TWG includes WHO EUD SPC WFP PIFS and others. Chaired by WHO.TECCBUF As specific TWG was not established because of the nature of the programme but the following stakeholders PIFS and EUD.Investment Facility for the Pacific was handled directly by the EUD.The FAs were all signed by December 2020. 2018 By the end of the third quarter 6 Financing Agreements were signed. IFP PEUMP PacWaste PPEVAW TECCBUF and PFM. 1 x ADs were consulted and drafted PRISE ongoing from 2017.2019 2 Programme ADs were consulted and approved PRISE ongoing from 2018 and IFP 2nd. 2020 1 x AD consulted and drafted Health Support Programme in Response to COVID in the Pacific 2x ADs approved. 3xFAs were signed PRISE IFP and Health Support Programme. With he approval and signature of these a final FAs 100 of the PRIP allocation was committed to the region.Every contracts between EU and ADB were pending conclusion of overarching agreement between both parties.
